card.keepWhy: She asked for them, and pointed to him.
sources: John 2:1-11 (the wedding at Cana in Galilee; the mother of Jesus is there; the wine fails; “They have no wine”; “Woman, what is that to me and to thee? my hour is not yet come”; “Whatsoever he shall say to you, do ye”; six stone waterpots for purification, two or three measures each; filled to the brim; the chief steward tastes: “thou hast kept the good wine until now”; the first of his signs).

Catechism of the Catholic Church 2132 (veneration of images), 954-962 (communion of saints), 971 (devotion to Mary differs essentially from the adoration given to God), 2618 (Mary’s intercession at Cana), 2683 (the saints’ intercession).
Comparative note: many Protestants honor Mary and the saints as examples but direct prayer to God alone; Orthodox Christians also ask the prayers of Mary and the saints.
check: The wine running out as a public shame for the hosts: widely taught, based on first-century hospitality customs; confirm the wording.
The lesson calls “Do whatever he tells you” Mary’s message at Cana and the line Catholics hold up; confirm this framing of Catholic teaching (cf. CCC 2618, 2674).
Comparative line on Protestant and Orthodox views is simplified; confirm.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? has someone ever noticed you needed help before you said a word?
options: then you’ll know the woman in this story. listen.
hold that friend in mind. this one is about noticing.
I’m usually the one who notices
then this story might feel like yours. listen.

steps.line: In the village of Cana there was a wedding. Mary was there, and Jesus and his friends were invited too.
In the middle of the feast, the wine ran out. For the young family, it would be a public embarrassment.

steps.q: Someone notices. Who, and what do they do?
o: The groom, who sends a servant to buy more
Mary, who quietly tells her son
The steward, who waters down what’s left
steps.why: Mary notices. She doesn’t fix it herself. She goes to her son.

steps.line: Mary noticed. She went to her son and said simply, “They have no wine.”
He said his hour had not yet come. Mary turned to the servants anyway: “Do whatever he tells you.”

steps.q: Jesus answers his mother, “Woman, what is that to you and to me?” Was calling her “Woman” rude?
o: Yes, he was putting her in her place
No, it was a respectful way to speak
It was a private nickname between them
steps.why: Many scholars say it was polite then, more like “ma’am,” though unusual from a son. John has Jesus call her that once more, at the cross: “Woman, here is your son.”

steps.line: Nearby stood six big stone jars for washing. He told the servants to fill them with water. They filled them to the brim.

steps.q: The servants carry a cup to the head steward. What does he say when he tastes it?
o: Where did this come from? Bring more
You’ve kept the best wine until now
steps.why: Water had become wine, and better than what they started with.

steps.line: The steward tasted it. The water had become wine. “Everyone serves the good wine first,” he said. “You’ve kept the best until now.”

steps.q: John doesn’t call this a miracle. He calls it the first of Jesus’s “signs.” Why that word?
o: It was too small to count as a miracle
It points past itself to who he is
Only the servants ever saw it happen
steps.why: John 2:11 says that here Jesus “revealed his glory, and his disciples believed in him.” A sign isn’t the point; it points.

steps.line: Today, candles flicker in front of a statue of Mary in many churches. Catholics aren’t praying to the statue. They’re asking her: pray for me.
steps.label: today

say: here’s the one difference. catholics give worship to God alone. mary and the saints get honor, the way you’d honor a grandmother, and they’re asked for their prayers, the way you’d ask a friend.

catholics call it the communion of saints: one family, living and dead, still praying for each other. orthodox christians ask the saints’ prayers too; many protestants honor them as examples and pray to God directly.

steps.q: Those little candles are called votive candles. What did the Latin word votum mean?
o: A vow, or a prayer offered
steps.why: Votum means a vow or an offered prayer. The candle keeps burning after you walk away, like the prayer you left with her.

steps.q: At Cana, Mary’s words were “Do whatever he tells you.” For Catholics, where does asking Mary for help lead a person?
o: To the statue instead of the person
steps.why: At Cana she sends everyone to Jesus. Catholics say she still does: honor her, and she points you to him.

today.say: if it feels right, ask one friend today to keep you in their prayers, or tell someone you’ll keep them in yours. that’s the communion of saints, in small. your choice.
options: that takes a little courage. it’s exactly what mary was asked.
that counts. noticing comes first, just like mary.
